AssertionError: 'StagedPathWithASpaceTest' not found in '# CI is the only definition of done. SEEN-086 runs the harness's own tests on
# the version floor; SEEN-089 extends this with typecheck, migrations, coverage,
# gitleaks, pnpm audit and graphify once there is product code to run them on.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
  pull_request:

jobs:
  harness:
    name: Harness tests (Python 3.12)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # doctor asks git which journal records were ever committed as a
          # modification, which a shallow clone cannot answer.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Harness tests
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s harness/tests -v

      # core.hooksPath is a per-clone setting, so a fresh checkout has none and
      # doctor rightly says so. Setting it here is the same single command a
      # person runs after cloning.
      - name: Wire up the git hooks
        run: git config core.hooksPath .githooks

      - name: Harness self-check
        run: python3 harness/run.py doctor

      # Every rule of the set says what it stands on, in both directions: a rule a
      # tool enables that rules/registry.toml does not carry fails here, and so
      # does a registry entry for a rule nothing runs (SEEN-114). It reads files
      # and needs no workspace, which is why it is in this job and the fixture
      # proof is in the one that installs.
      - name: Every rule in the set is traceable
        run: python3 harness/run.py rules --check

  secrets:
    name: Secrets and supply chain
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # Full history: a credential is findable in an old commit, not only
          # at the tip, and that is exactly the one nobody remembers.
          fetch-depth: 0

      # The CLI rather than the action: the action enumerates pull request
      # commits through the API and fails on the token's permissions before it
      # scans anything, which reports a secrets failure that has nothing to do
      # with secrets. The binary needs no API and scans the same history the
      # pre-commit hook scans staged changes against.
      - name: gitleaks
        run: |
          version=8.30.1
          curl -sSL "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v${version}/gitleaks_${version}_linux_x64.tar.gz" \
            | tar -xz gitleaks
          ./gitleaks git . --redact --no-banner

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # A high advisory with no fix available still fails. Waiving one is a
      # decision recorded in the ticket that waives it, not a flag here.
      - name: Audit
        run: pnpm audit --audit-level high

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: No live marketplace host in test code
        run: python3 harness/run.py lint

  node:
    name: Monorepo (Node 24)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    # No service containers. The tests talk to real Redis, Mailpit, a collector
    # and Supabase, and they are started from docker-compose.yml and
    # supabase/config.toml, the same two files `pnpm dev:up` reads on a laptop.
    # Restating the images here is how the two definitions drift (SEEN-097).
    env:
      REDIS_HOST: 127.0.0.1
      REDIS_PORT: 6379
      SMTP_HOST: 127.0.0.1
      SMTP_PORT: 1025
      MAILPIT_URL: http://127.0.0.1:8025
      SEEN_OTLP_ENDPOINT: http://127.0.0.1:4318
      SUPABASE_URL: http://127.0.0.1:54321

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: pnpm

      # Frozen: a lockfile that drifts in CI is a lockfile that proves nothing.
      - name: Install
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # The rule set's fixtures and `harness rules` are Python over installed
      # tools, so this job needs both. The harness job has Python and no
      # workspace; this one has the workspace and needed Python.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - uses: supabase/setup-cli@v1
        with:
          version: 2.116.0

      - name: Start Redis, Mailpit and the collector
        run: docker compose up -d --wait

      # Studio mounts this directory and docker chowns a mount source it creates
      # itself, which some mounts deny. dev:up does the same on a laptop.
      - name: Start Supabase
        run: |
          mkdir -p supabase/snippets
          supabase start

      # Each rule against the fixture it stands on, before the set is pointed at
      # real code: a rule that does not refuse its own fixture is a rule nothing
      # proves, and a green tree would otherwise read as though it had been
      # judged (SEEN-114).
      - name: Every rule refuses its own fixture
        run: python3 harness/run.py rules --fixtures

      # The per-package lint, which is Biome through turbo's cache and is what a
      # developer runs.
      - name: Lint
        run: pnpm turbo run lint

      # The whole rule set over the tree, which adds the three tools turbo's
      # per-package lint does not run: ast-grep, dependency-cruiser and knip.
      # Biome runs twice across the two steps, which costs about 300ms and keeps
      # each entry point whole: the hook, this step and the per-package script
      # all read one configuration, and splitting the tools between them would
      # be the drift SEEN-097 recorded.
      - name: The rule set on the tree
        run: ./scripts/rules.sh tree

      - name: Typecheck
        run: pnpm turbo run typecheck

      - name: Test
        run: pnpm turbo run test

      - name: Build
        run: pnpm turbo run build

      # Leaves the runner as it found it, and prints what failed when something did.
      - name: Stop the stack
        if: always()
        run: |
          supabase stop --no-backup || true
          docker compose logs --tail 50 || true
          docker compose down || true

  graph:
    name: Knowledge graph
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Install graphify
        run: pip install --quiet graphifyy

      # Code extraction only: local, deterministic, no API key and no token
      # spend per build. The semantic pass over documents uses a model and is
      # run deliberately, not on every push.
      - name: Extract the graph
        run: graphify extract . --code-only

      # graphify writes node-link JSON, so the edges are under "links".
      - name: The graph must parse
        run: |
          python3 -c "import json; g = json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json')); \
            links = g.get('links', g.get('edges', [])); \
            print(f\"{len(g['nodes'])} nodes, {len(links)} edges\"); \
            assert g['nodes'] and links, 'the graph is empty'"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: graph-report
          path: |
            graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md
            graphify-out/graph.json
'
